newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - PacifiCorp eyed Energy since demerger.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - PacifiCorp eyed Energy since demerger.

text.p: PacifiCorp and Energy Group Plc have been exploring a combination since the British company was demerged from Hanson Plc in February, PacifiCorp's chief executive said Friday .
"Our discussions started about the time of the demerger, exploring whether it made sense," CEO Frederick Buckman told Reuters in a telephone interview.
He said he expects PacifiCorp's $9.6 billion acquisition of Energy Group, announced earlier today, to close by late summer or early autumn.

"We have been following both Eastern, (Energy Group's) electric and gas marketing and distribution arm in the U.K., since mid-1995, and we have known Peabody (Energy Group's coal mining unit) for a long time," Buckman said.

He declined to comment on whether Portland, Ore.-based PacifiCorp would change its dividend policy, but said the board will consider the issue "prior to the close of the transaction" with Energy Group.
PacifiCorp shares currently pay an annual dividend of $1.08 per common share, producing a yield of almost 4.9 percent.
Energy Group is "very well respected in coal mining and in the operation of (generating) plants and (electric) distribution," Buckman said.
"But their two businesses are not well connected. By putting these two businesses together, we accomplish a significant step in the strategy of PacifiCorp," he said.

"We are developing a philosophy shared by a few other companies in the world...looking at coal as solid electricity and natural gas as a gaseous form of electricity, and the railroads and gas pipelines comparable to electric transmission systems," the PacifiCorp CEO said.
Asked about the application of electric power trading techniques, such as arbitrage, to the fuel markets, he said:

"One of the ways to be successful in the marketing and trading of energy is have access to physical assets (like coal and natural gas), so you can take advantage of imperfections in the marketplace to meet customer needs."

On earnings, Buckman declined to elaborate on the company's earlier statement that the merger would be "meaningfully accretive" to PacifiCorp earnings in the first year after completion of the deal and thereafter, before any saving from potential cost cuts and revenue enhancements.

Energy Group, previously part of Hanson, became an independent company in February. Its Eastern unit is the largest British regional electric company, with 3.1 million retail electric and gas customers.
PacifiCorp has 1.4 million retail electric customers in the western U.S. and 550,000 in the State of Victoria, Australia.
Together, the companies will have five million retail electric customers, annual sales revenue of $11.5 billion, and 10.3 billion tons of coal reserves.
